subject.title: [Feature]: Include interaction metadata in Discord button callbacks

question: Should generic Discord component callbacks expose a new agent-visible structured interaction metadata envelope, and which fields are safe public contract versus plugin-only callback data?
rationale: The change would expose Discord identifiers and callback data through a public agent inbound-context contract, so automation should not choose the schema or trust boundary.

options.title: Add Bounded Metadata
options.body: Expose documented safe fields such as component kind, originating message id, selected values, label, and clicker identity, with callback/custom data only in a maintainer-approved shape.

options.title: Keep Generic Callbacks Text-Only
options.body: Leave richer interaction fields on plugin interactive handlers and document generic callbacks as label/value text for compatibility.

options.title: Start With Sender And Message
options.body: Expose only clicker identity and originating message id first, deferring callback payload semantics until a broader inbound metadata contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Add Bounded Metadata
recommendation.body: Expose documented safe fields such as component kind, originating message id, selected values, label, and clicker identity, with callback/custom data only in a maintainer-approved shape.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history around Discord component wiring, plugin SDK boundaries, and inbound context refactors where this public contract would likely be shaped.
